Accoya Wood for Driveway Gates

Understand modified timber, gate construction, coating care and the difference between material and installation warranties.

On this page +
What Accoya isAssess the finished gateRead each warranty separatelyCompare like-for-like alternatives

What Accoya is

Accoya starts as softwood and undergoes acetylation, a modification process. It is not a naturally occurring hardwood or a chemical-free treatment. Read the manufacturer’s material explanation when comparing it with other timber options.

Specify the actual wood product in the quotation. The appearance of a finished gate also depends on its boards, joints, frame and coating.

Assess the finished gate

Ask how the joiner has designed the gate for its width, weight and movement. Discuss the supports, fittings and exposure alongside the timber choice. Material properties alone cannot guarantee that a complete gate will never move, split or need adjustment.

View a finish sample beside the property. Decide whether you want a painted surface, visible grain or a weathered appearance, and request the care schedule for that choice.

Read each warranty separately

Request the current manufacturer terms for the supplied material and the separate terms for fabrication, finish, fittings, installation and automation. Confirm what a claim covers, exclusions, records required and any labour charges.

A timber warranty does not automatically cover coatings, hinges or the workmanship of a finished gate. Check the documents linked from Accoya’s ownership guidance against the proposed application.

Compare like-for-like alternatives

Use the same dimensions, board layout, finish and automation scope to compare Accoya with other wooden gates. Our timber and aluminium comparison includes wood-effect options. Ask for product availability and written terms before deciding.

Choosing Anthracite Grey for Driveway Gates

Compare colour samples, sheen and surrounding materials before specifying an anthracite gate finish.

Use a physical sample

Ask for the proposed coating colour reference, sheen and texture on the actual gate material. A screen image changes with display settings and lighting. Two finishes described as anthracite can look different beside brick, stone or render.

Place a sample outside in sun and shade. Check it beside existing window frames and doors rather than assuming that the same colour name guarantees a visual match.

Specify the complete entrance

Include gate leaves, posts, hinges, visible motor covers and the pedestrian entrance in the finish schedule. Ask which components come from different manufacturers and whether slight variations are expected.

For a wood-effect or two-tone design, inspect the joint between finishes and the rear face. Request a drawing showing the areas to receive each finish.

Compare upkeep and repair options

Ask for cleaning instructions, touch-up advice and written coating terms. Dark colour alone does not establish how much dust will show or how long the finish will last. Avoid choosing on unsourced trend or maintenance percentages.

Compare aluminium and other metal gates using the actual construction and coating specification. Bring your preferred sample when you discuss your entrance.

Article 4 Directions and Driveway Gate Planning Permission

Check the mapped property and the rights withdrawn by a direction before changing your front boundary.

On this page +
Read the direction for the addressCheck other controls separatelyPrepare a clear enquiry

Read the direction for the address

An Article 4 direction removes specified permitted development rights in a defined area or at specified properties. Its existence somewhere in a borough does not establish the rules for your gate. Obtain the actual direction, map, schedule and effective date from the planning authority.

Check whether the withdrawn rights cover the proposed boundary work. Camden’s Article 4 directory separates different kinds of directions and links to the relevant records; use your own authority’s equivalent.

Check other controls separately

Conservation-area designation, listed status and conditions on earlier planning permissions are separate checks. The position beside a highway and the proposed height can also affect the gate proposal. A neighbour’s replacement gate is not proof that your work is permitted.

Start with the council planning directory and general gate planning guidance. Ask the authority which information it needs for your address.

Prepare a clear enquiry

Provide a site plan, photographs of the existing boundary and a drawing of the proposed gate, pillars and opening direction. Include dimensions, materials and any excavation, paving or access changes.

Ask whether a formal application, consent or certificate is appropriate. Retain the written response and any conditions with the quotation. Set the installation programme after the required checks.

Electric Driveway Gates and Home Insurance

Ask your insurer how an automated gate affects your policy instead of assuming a premium discount or automatic cover.

On this page +
Ask about your own policyClarify what damage and costs are coveredKeep useful records

Ask about your own policy

There is no insurance discount we can promise for adding a driveway gate. Contact your insurer or broker before relying on the gate as a policy security measure. Describe the proposed installation and any change to property access.

Ask whether you need to notify them when the work is complete and whether the policy contains conditions about operation, locking or maintenance. Request confirmation that you can keep with your policy documents.

Clarify what damage and costs are covered

Ask how the policy treats the gate, motors, controls and underground services. Discuss accidental impact, storm or flood damage, electrical faults, wear, theft and the applicable excesses. These are questions for the insurer, not a list of guaranteed cover.

Check whether a damaged gate that blocks the entrance requires a particular claims process before you arrange repairs. A product warranty and an insurance policy cover different risks.

Keep useful records

Retain the quotation, installed product details, invoice, handover information and service records. Take photographs of the completed entrance and record changes to the equipment.

Automated Gates on Sloping Driveways in London

Compare the questions a survey must resolve on a sloping driveway, including movement space, supports, drainage and safe manual operation.

On this page +
Measure the slope where the gate will moveQuestions for a swing-gate layoutQuestions for a sliding layoutPlan for manual release and uncontrolled movementSupports, groundworks and permissionsWhat to request with the quoteFAQs

Measure the slope where the gate will move

A driveway can rise or fall across the entrance, along the drive, or both. The survey needs to establish the actual levels, movement area, boundary position and where vehicles and people will wait. A photograph or one gradient figure cannot establish a suitable design.

Tell the installer about drainage problems, previous ground movement and any changes planned to paving or parking. These details can affect the gate layout and the order of the work.

Questions for a swing-gate layout

A swing gate needs clearance through its full movement. If the ground rises behind the entrance, the leaf may meet the surface or leave a changing gap. The assessment should consider the hinge arrangement, supports, parked vehicles and risks created by the movement.

Do not assume a rising hinge or a more powerful motor resolves the problem. Ask the installer to explain the proposed geometry and protective measures. Compare electric swing-gate options after the site constraints are understood.

Questions for a sliding layout

A sliding gate requires a suitable travel path and room beside the opening. Tracked, cantilever and multi-panel arrangements have different support and space requirements. The survey should assess levels, drainage, foundations and the surroundings along that path.

A sliding design is not automatically suitable merely because a driveway slopes. Request a drawing showing movement and clearances. Discuss sliding-gate installation with the actual site measurements.

Plan for manual release and uncontrolled movement

Gravity or wind can move a gate when it is freed from its drive. The design must account for safe operation and the circumstances in which manual release is used. Ask how the gate is controlled and secured, and which situations require an engineer.

Keep people and vehicles clear of a gate that moves unexpectedly. Do not disengage a damaged or unstable gate to see whether it rolls or swings. Follow the installed system’s user instructions; a generic release sequence cannot account for your slope.

Supports, groundworks and permissions

Foundation dimensions, reinforcement and drainage need to suit the proposed gate and site. Do not use a standard depth, rebar spacing or weight threshold from a web article as the construction design. The contractor should identify any specialist structural or ground advice needed.

Check applicable planning and highway constraints before ordering. Gate width alone does not provide a universal planning-permission test. Consult Planning Portal guidance on gates and boundaries and the authority responsible for the property.

What to request with the quote

Ask for the gate layout, material, supports, drive, protective measures, drainage, electrical work and surface reinstatement to be identified. Confirm work required from other trades and the checks, documents and training included at handover.

Use our installed-cost checklist to compare scope, then request a survey. The safety basis is a site-specific assessment; see HSE guidance on powered-gate safety.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a sloping driveway have electric gates?+
A suitable arrangement may be possible, but it depends on measured levels, space, supports, movement and the safety assessment. A survey should establish the options.
Are sliding gates always the answer on a slope?+
No. The travel path, side space, support arrangement and surroundings still need assessment. Compare actual layouts rather than choosing from the gradient alone.
Can stronger motors compensate for a poor layout?+
Do not treat motor power as a substitute for suitable geometry, supports and protective measures. The complete system needs assessment.

Bi-fold vs Sliding Gates for Short Driveways

Compare folding clearance and sliding run-back space without relying on a universal opening-speed or space-saving claim.

On this page +
Compare two different movement pathsCheck folding joints and side spaceInclude slopes and everyday accessGet comparable proposals

Compare two different movement paths

Bi-fold leaves fold as they swing, reducing the depth occupied by some designs compared with a single full-length swing leaf. Sliding gates move alongside the opening and need a clear path beside it. Both arrangements need supports and space for their moving parts.

For a short drive, draw the parked vehicle, its doors, the gate’s entire movement and a pedestrian route. Ask the installer to mark the dimensions of the actual mechanism rather than applying a percentage saving from another product.

Check folding joints and side space

Folding designs need assessment around intermediate hinges and the area where the panels gather. Sliding designs need assessment along the run-back area and between the leaf and nearby walls or fencing.

If one sliding leaf will not fit beside the entrance, compare telescopic panels. More panels change the support, movement and maintenance requirements; they do not make the surrounding space irrelevant.

Include slopes and everyday access

Ground levels may interfere with a folding swing path or require changes to a sliding layout. Discuss drainage, parked-car position, visitors and bins. Ask what happens during manual release, particularly on a slope.

Opening time depends on the selected equipment, travel and safe operation. Do not choose a layout on a universal two-second promise. A demonstration should show the proposed arrangement, including its stopping and closing behaviour.

Get comparable proposals

Request drawings, product models, groundworks, protective measures and service arrangements for both options. Use the swing and sliding comparison for the broader layout questions, then compare the complete quotations using our installed gate cost guide.

Designing Driveway Gates in a Conservation Area

Use the actual conservation appraisal and property constraints to plan changes to a historic front boundary.

On this page +
Identify what gives the boundary its characterSeparate design choices from permissionConsider repair before replacementShow the complete proposed entrance

Identify what gives the boundary its character

Photograph the existing gate, railings, piers and adjacent frontage. Note original details you want to retain and damage that needs repair. Find the council’s conservation-area appraisal or management guidance for the actual address.

Avoid assuming that all period homes need the same metalwork, colour or dimensions. A new gate should be discussed in the context of that boundary and the applicable planning controls.

Separate design choices from permission

Check conservation designation, any Article 4 direction, listed status and existing conditions. Demolition or alteration of a boundary can raise a different question from adding automation. Ask the planning authority to identify the process for the complete proposal.

Our Article 4 guide explains how to read a direction. Use the council directory to locate the responsible authority.

Consider repair before replacement

Ask a suitable metalworker or joiner to assess the existing gate and supports. Retaining sound fabric may be an option, but condition and safe operation must guide the proposal. Compare repair, replacement and automation as separate pieces of work.

Our metal-gate restoration guide covers material identification and finish questions. Do not remove historic features before the necessary advice or consent.

Show the complete proposed entrance

Drawings should show gate proportions, infill, pillars, finish and opening path. Include visible controls, cable routes, drainage and groundworks. A concealed motor still needs foundations and maintenance access.

Agree who obtains permissions and which approved details govern fabrication. Compare the quotation against those drawings before ordering.

Further reading: Planning Portal gate and boundary guidance.

Check vehicle-crossing approval separately from gate planning, paving and ownership permissions.

A gate does not authorise driving across a pavement

If vehicles will cross a public footway to reach the property, check the vehicle-crossing requirements with the highway authority. An existing opening, gravel drive or gate is not proof that the crossing is approved.

Use the GOV.UK dropped-kerb service to find the relevant council. Ask about an existing crossing as well as a proposed new or widened one.

Show the complete access arrangement

Provide photographs, the property address and a plan showing the gate, parking space, road and pavement. Identify street trees, utility covers, lamps and other features near the proposed crossing.

Ask the authority for its current eligibility rules, application process, approved work arrangements and charges. Do not book pavement work on the basis of another borough’s dimensions or a generic online price.

Keep the permissions separate

Check planning requirements for the gate and entrance, highway approval for the crossing, and ownership or lease restrictions. The responsible authority should confirm which processes apply to your address and road.

Paving and drainage need their own design. Read our front-garden paving guide and include approved crossover work and surface reinstatement in the installed gate cost guide.

Will Driveway Gates Reduce Traffic Noise?

Consider the complete boundary and the location of the noise before buying gates for acoustic performance.

On this page +
Do not budget on an untested decibel claimAssess the whole frontageCheck design trade-offs

Do not budget on an untested decibel claim

A gate may change the openness of the front boundary, but its appearance and weight do not establish a particular reduction in traffic noise. Sound can reach the property around and above the entrance, through gaps and by routes unrelated to the gate.

Ask for acoustic evidence that fits the actual proposal before paying for a promised numerical improvement. A result from another property cannot establish the outcome at yours.

Assess the whole frontage

Show an acoustic adviser the road, gate position, adjoining walls, ground levels and the windows or garden area you want to protect. Explain when the disturbance occurs and whether the gate would be open during those periods.

Gate, fence and planting claims cannot simply be added together into a total reduction. Consider the boundary as a whole and compare practical options for the particular source and receiving location.

Check design trade-offs

A closed gate affects views, airflow and wind exposure, and must still provide a suitable entrance for people and vehicles. Ask the gate installer to coordinate any acoustic proposal with the supports, movement and protective measures.

Choose gate materials and layout for the complete entrance. If noise reduction is the main objective, obtain the acoustic assessment before ordering a gate on that promise.

Parcel and Delivery Access Through Electric Gates

Choose a delivery routine that works when you are home, away or unable to answer an intercom.

Choose where parcels should goManage codes and visitor callsKeep movement and access separateChoose the equipment around the routine

Choose where parcels should go

Decide whether a courier should enter the driveway or leave a parcel at an accessible delivery point outside the powered gate. Give clear instructions that do not require climbing, reaching through the gate or leaving goods in its movement path.

Consider pedestrian access and the position of a parcel box before adding an entry device. A delivery routine should also work when you cannot answer a call.

Manage codes and visitor calls

A keypad can offer temporary or separately managed codes if the selected product supports them. Check how codes expire and how you remove access. Avoid placing a permanent household code in public delivery notes.

A video or phone intercom lets you speak with the visitor, subject to the installed connection and app features. Notifications, recordings and remote release vary by model and account. Request a demonstration rather than assuming they are included.

Keep movement and access separate

Letting a visitor in does not confirm that the gate’s path is clear. The installation needs protective measures for the actual entrance, and users need instructions on where to wait and move. Do not ask a courier to hold a powered leaf open or obstruct a sensor.

Agree an alternative for network or power failure. Keep manual release to trained users following the supplied instructions, rather than sharing a generic release sequence with delivery drivers.

Choose the equipment around the routine

Compare keypad access, video entry and phone entry. Check account ownership and recurring charges in the quotation. Our gate safety guide explains the handover information to request.

Keep the system maintainable

Why Your Gate Motor Is Humming but Not Moving

A humming gate motor needs diagnosis. Learn what you can observe safely, when to stop using the gate and what to tell a repair engineer.

On this page +
Stop repeated attempts to open the gateWhat can cause a humming gate motor?Useful observations without dismantling anythingManual release is specific to your systemWhat to ask the repair engineerAfter the repairFAQs

Stop repeated attempts to open the gate

If the motor hums but the gate does not move, stop pressing the remote or entry control. The sound does not identify one particular fault, and repeated attempts can place further strain on the system. Keep people and vehicles clear of the gate and its movement area.

If there is smoke, a burning smell, damaged wiring, a leaning gate or unexpected movement, stop using the entrance. Use the isolation arrangements in your user instructions only if you can reach and operate them safely. Do not open electrical covers or approach damaged equipment. Contact an engineer; if someone is trapped or there is immediate danger, call the emergency services.

What can cause a humming gate motor?

An obstruction, a mechanical problem, a drive fault or an electrical supply/control problem can prevent movement. A damaged hinge, wheel or running gear can change the load on the motor. Some motor designs also have components that can fail while the motor still makes a noise.

An engineer needs the actual equipment details and an assessment of the complete entrance to distinguish these causes. Motor voltage, capacitor requirements and diagnostic readings vary by system. A generic internet voltage figure or replacement part is not a reliable diagnosis.

Useful observations without dismantling anything

From a safe position, note whether one leaf or both are affected, whether the problem happens when opening or closing, and which normal user control you tried. Record when the problem started and whether a power interruption, vehicle impact or recent work preceded it. Do not recreate an unsafe movement to obtain a video.

Look for visible debris in a track, a displaced gate or a damaged fitting without entering a trapping zone or touching moving parts. If the system has a user display, note the message according to its instructions. These observations help the engineer plan a visit; they are not a reason to remove guards or test exposed terminals.

Manual release is specific to your system

Follow the supplied user instructions and handover training if you need to use manual release. A released gate can move under wind, gravity or its own weight. Do not release a damaged or unstable gate, or try to push a gate that resists movement.

If you do not know how to control and secure it, keep the area clear and ask for assistance. Our manual-release guide explains what information to check before acting. Never bypass a safety device to get the entrance working.

What to ask the repair engineer

Send your postcode, a description of the fault and any safely accessible model details. Share maintenance records and photographs of the entrance taken from a safe position. Mention whether the gate is stuck open or closed and whether it affects access to the property.

Ask what the diagnostic visit covers, what it costs and how further work will be approved. The findings should explain the cause, any wider safety concern, the proposed repair and how the system will be checked before being returned to use. Electrical testing, capacitor work, control adjustments and powered movement tests belong with a competent person.

Request gate repair and maintenance, or read our advice on changing gate repair companies if records or support are missing.

After the repair

Keep the diagnosis, parts information and service records with the gate instructions. Ask the engineer to explain any changed operating arrangements and the recommended maintenance for your equipment. Confirm the repair warranty in writing rather than assuming it matches the original installation cover.

Source: HSE guidance on responsibilities. A humming noise alone does not establish whether a repair or replacement is needed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I keep trying the remote?+
Stop repeated attempts when the motor runs or hums without moving the gate. Keep clear and arrange assessment rather than trying to force operation.
Does humming mean the capacitor has failed?+
Not necessarily. Causes vary with the motor and installation. A competent engineer needs to diagnose the fault; do not open the motor or replace electrical parts from a generic online suggestion.
Can you assess gates installed by another company?+
Send the equipment details and fault description so we can discuss an assessment. Confirm the visit scope and charges before booking.

GSM Gate Openers: Network, SIM and Access Checks

Check phone-entry compatibility, signal, SIM costs and account ownership before adding a mobile gate opener.

On this page +
Separate phone entry from visitor callingCheck the device, SIM and network togetherSurvey the signal and ongoing costsHand over access management

Separate phone entry from visitor calling

Some gate controllers recognise an authorised phone number and request an opening when it calls. An intercom also lets a visitor speak to a resident. Ask which function the proposed device provides, whether it uses voice, SMS or data, and what the caller experiences.

A remote command does not confirm that the entrance is clear or the gate has opened. Discuss how the complete system manages unattended operation and how you will know whether a fault has prevented movement.

Check the device, SIM and network together

Ask for the exact device model and supported network technologies. Confirm the SIM plan permits its required services and how the unit handles caller identification. A label saying 4G does not, by itself, confirm support for the voice service your network uses.

Mobile operators are retiring older networks. Check Ofcom’s current switch-off guidance and obtain the equipment supplier’s migration advice. Avoid buying an older controller solely because a SIM currently connects.

Survey the signal and ongoing costs

Test service at the gate position on the proposed network. Discuss the enclosure, antenna location, cable route and power supply with the installer. Nearby buildings and the installed position can affect the result.

Confirm monthly charges, call or data allowances, top-up rules and what happens if an account expires. Ask whose name holds the SIM and how the household can change numbers or recover administrator access.

Hand over access management

Request a demonstration of adding and removing authorised users using the actual manual. Remove default credentials, restrict administrator access and arrange a backup entry method. Keep account recovery information with your gate records.

For installation, see GSM phone entry. Compare visitor workflows in our intercom guide. A failing controller belongs in a repair assessment rather than a generic SMS reset sequence.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will any UK SIM work?+
No universal compatibility claim is reliable. Check the device, network, required voice/SMS/data services and tariff restrictions together.

Planning and vehicle access are separate checks

Gate height, listed status, withdrawn rights and the boundary work can affect planning requirements. A dropped kerb or vehicle crossing involves a separate highway enquiry. One approval does not settle all those matters.

Tree Preservation Orders and Driveway Gate Groundworks

Check protected-tree constraints before planning gate posts, foundations, drainage or cable routes near front-garden trees.

On this page +
Check the tree and proposed work before excavationWhat a Tree Preservation Order can restrictConservation-area trees need a separate checkGive the adviser the full entrance layoutAgree the method and responsibilities in writingPrepare the enquiry and compare the scopeFAQs

Check the tree and proposed work before excavation

Gate posts, foundations, tracks, drainage and cable routes can affect nearby trees as well as the entrance. Start by identifying the trees and discussing the proposed work with the local planning authority and a competent arboricultural adviser where needed.

Check Tree Preservation Orders, conservation-area status and relevant conditions on existing planning permissions. Do not assume permission for a gate authorises all work affecting a tree.

What a Tree Preservation Order can restrict

A Tree Preservation Order protects specified trees, groups or woodlands. Government guidance identifies prohibited activities without the authority’s written consent, including cutting down, topping, lopping, uprooting, wilful damage and destruction. It also explains that cutting roots can require consent.

The work, exemptions and procedure need checking for the actual circumstances. Consult GOV.UK guidance on protected trees and the relevant local authority before carrying out work.

Conservation-area trees need a separate check

A tree can be subject to conservation-area controls even where it is not covered by a Tree Preservation Order. Notification requirements and exceptions depend on the circumstances. Ask the council which process applies and allow for it before agreeing a start date.

A borough label or generic website statement cannot confirm the status of your tree. Keep the authority’s response, any consent and its conditions with the project records.

Give the adviser the full entrance layout

Show the proposed gate, supports, motor or track, power cable, drainage and paving changes. Include temporary construction access, storage and vehicle movements. An excavation outside the visible canopy is not automatically clear of roots.

Ask the arboricultural adviser and gate contractor to coordinate the required protection area, access restrictions and construction method. Do not substitute a simple trunk-distance formula or a permitted percentage of root loss for that assessment.

Agree the method and responsibilities in writing

The proposal should identify who will obtain information or consent, which work is permitted, the protection arrangements and any supervision required. Where the layout needs to change to avoid harm, update the gate drawings and quotation before construction.

This article does not prescribe air-spading pressures, root barriers or a universal foundation detail. Those choices need site-specific advice. Do not cut exposed roots or alter the agreed method to keep a gate job moving; stop the affected work and obtain advice.

Prepare the enquiry and compare the scope

Send the property location, photographs from accessible positions and a description of the entrance work you want. Share tree reports, council responses and existing plans if you have them. Ask which specialist work falls within the gate quotation and which needs a separate appointment.

Our gate quotation checklist helps identify exclusions. Discuss the gate project before commissioning equipment that may not fit the agreed protected-tree layout.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a gate project need checks for nearby tree roots?+
Yes. Foundations, tracks, cables, drainage and construction access can affect roots. Check protected status and obtain competent advice for the proposed work before excavation.
Does gate planning permission automatically allow root cutting?+
Do not assume that it does. Ask the local authority which permissions, tree consents, conditions or notifications apply to the actual work.
Can I use a standard distance from the trunk for the gate post?+
A generic distance is not a site design. Ask the relevant adviser and contractor to establish the protection and construction arrangements for the tree and entrance.

Compare samples at your property

Timber has natural grain and variation; painted aluminium gives a more uniform surface. Wood-effect aluminium offers a printed or applied timber appearance, but grain repetition, edges and the rear face can look different from real wood.

View samples beside your brickwork in daylight and shade. Ask to see the finish on a corner, joint and reverse face, rather than choosing from a small photograph. Check how the posts, pedestrian gate and fencing will match.

Look beyond the face of the gate

For timber, ask for the species or modified-wood product, board construction, frame joints and finish specification. For aluminium, ask about the frame, infill, joints, coating and repair options. The material name alone does not establish stiffness, durability or suitability for automation.

Separate the timber or coating warranty from the gate fabrication, installation and automation terms. Ask about exclusions, maintenance records and labour charges. A raw-material warranty does not promise that the complete gate will remain unchanged for that period.

Put the same opening dimensions, infill, finish, supports, automation and access controls into both quotations. Include removal of the old entrance, power, groundworks, VAT and reinstatement. This gives you a useful comparison without relying on a universal lifespan or percentage saving.

List who should receive a call and whether they need an indoor monitor, phone calls, an app or a combination. Include anyone who does not use a smartphone. Decide what happens if nobody answers and how a visitor can leave a delivery.

Ask for a demonstration of the actual sequence: call, identify the visitor, grant entry and confirm that the gate has finished moving. Seeing a video does not necessarily mean the app reports the gate’s physical position.

Compare the connection paths

A wired indoor system can suit a household that wants a dedicated answering point. An IP system needs the specified network and power arrangements. A mobile-network intercom needs suitable coverage, device support and a compatible SIM plan.

Test the connection at the proposed gate position. A strong indoor Wi-Fi signal or a phone signal from another network does not prove the intercom will work there. Discuss what remains available during a broadband, mobile-service or power failure.

Get the exact equipment and account terms

Request model numbers, the proposed release interface, supported monitors and app requirements. Confirm recording options, retention, subscriptions, SIM charges and which account owns the system. Ask how to remove a former resident or contractor.

Product families contain different devices. Compare named configurations rather than assuming a brand guarantees compatibility. Our Comelit and Hikvision comparison shows why the component list matters.

Plan installation and support

Include cable routes, power, camera position, lighting, accessibility and weather exposure in the survey. Confirm who commissions the connection to the gate controller and checks operation of the complete entrance.

Compare video intercoms and phone entry. For an existing smart-home setup, use our integration checklist. Check Ofcom’s network-retirement guidance before buying mobile-network equipment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which brand is best?+
Compare the proposed models against your wiring, visitor workflow, network, account costs and support requirements. A brand ranking cannot establish compatibility.
Does an app continue working during a power cut?+
That depends on backup power for the gate, intercom and network equipment, as well as the service connection. Ask for the actual failure arrangements.

Home/Guides/Electric Gate Costs
Pricing & CostsUpdated 2 October 2026

Electric Driveway Gate Costs in London

Compare the full cost of an electric driveway gate, from supply and groundworks to power, access controls and ongoing care.

On this page +
Start with the complete installed costThe items to include in your quotationHow gate material and opening layout affect the priceGroundworks, electrical supply and making goodNew installation and retrofit: two different scopesVAT, exclusions and payment stagesBudget for ownership as well as installationPrepare an enquiry that helps us quote

The cost of electric driveway gates depends on the entrance as well as the gate. A supply-only price leaves out work such as supports, electrical supply and installation. To set a useful budget, ask for a measured survey and an itemised quotation covering the complete job.

Start with the complete installed cost

A gate advertised at a particular price may include only the leaves or sliding panel. A motor-kit price may cover the motor and controller without the work needed to make the complete installation suitable for your site. Before comparing totals, establish whether each quotation covers the same opening, materials and work.

There is no single installed price that applies to every London driveway. Width and height, ground conditions, access for the installation team, existing pillars, the power route and your chosen entry controls can change the scope. A useful quotation identifies those items and states what remains subject to inspection.

For a new powered entrance, discuss a complete automated gate installation. For gates you intend to keep, start with an assessment for automating existing gates. The two projects need different quotations.

The items to include in your quotation

Part of the jobAsk the quotation to identify
Gate supplyDimensions, material, construction, finish, delivery and fittings.
Supports and groundworksPosts or pillar alterations, foundations, track or other support work, drainage and removal of waste.
AutomationMotor and controller models, installation, system-specific protective measures and commissioning.
Electrical workSupply assessment, cable route, required work and who provides the relevant test records.
Access controlsRemotes, intercom, keypad or phone entry, connectivity and ongoing charges.
Finishing and handoverReinstatement of paving or planting, removal of old equipment, user instructions and demonstration.
Price and termsVAT treatment, exclusions, allowances, payment stages, warranty and maintenance conditions.

Ask who supplies each item and who takes responsibility for the assembled installation. If separate trades are involved, agree the handover between them before work starts.

How gate material and opening layout affect the price

Compare the specified product rather than assuming one material will always cost less. Aluminium gates vary in profile construction and finish. Composite gates need a defined board-and-frame specification. With hardwood gates, the timber, joinery and coating affect the work and future care.

Bespoke dimensions and decorative fabrication can change the cost of a gate. Request the drawing and finish reference that match the price. Include the posts, hinges, locks and visible hardware in the comparison.

Swing and sliding layouts involve different support and movement arrangements. A sliding quotation needs the proposed track or cantilever support and space along the boundary. A swing quotation needs adequate movement space and suitable supports. Let the measured layout guide the choice, then compare the cost of suitable options.

Groundworks, electrical supply and making good

Ask the surveyor to trace the proposed power route and identify the surfaces that need to be lifted. A short route across a planted border and a route beneath finished paving involve different work. Agree who reinstates those surfaces and whether the quote includes matching materials or an allowance.

Existing pillars and foundations may need investigation before the installer can confirm that they are suitable. Discuss access for equipment, waste removal and any arrangements affecting neighbours or a shared driveway. Request a process for agreeing extra work if the team finds an issue after excavation.

Check planning or other permissions before committing to the work. Ask the relevant local authority about your particular boundary where restrictions may apply, and include any application or professional costs in your own budget. A contractor’s gate quotation does not automatically include these expenses.

New installation and retrofit: two different scopes

The following are scope comparisons, not completed projects or quoted prices.

A new gate and automated entrance

Compare gate supply, new or adapted supports, groundworks, power, motors, controls and finishing as one project. Ask which parts of the work the named contractor will complete and which require another trade. A low gate-supply figure does not establish the final installed total.

Automation added to existing gates

Ask the installer to assess the condition, movement and supports of the retained gates before pricing the motors. Repairs, altered hinges, new supports or other changes may be needed. The quotation should say which parts remain, which change and how the completed system will be assessed and handed over.

HSE’s powered-gate safety guidance explains why the gate, equipment and site need consideration together. Keep protective measures and commissioning in the scope when comparing prices.

VAT, exclusions and payment stages

Ask for the amount payable, whether it includes VAT and the basis for any exception. GOV.UK states that most building work on homes attracts the standard 20% rate, with exceptions. That does not establish the VAT status of an individual supplier or the treatment of your project; get both confirmed on the quotation.

Check whether quoted sums are fixed items or allowances that can change once details are known. Ask the contractor to list exclusions such as power work, old-gate disposal, replacement paving, permits or subscriptions. Agree how variations need your approval.

Keep the payment schedule with the specification. Confirm what each stage covers, the expected lead time and the arrangements if the scope or delivery date changes. If you consider finance from any provider, compare the total repayable and fees; this guide does not assume that gate finance is available from us.

Budget for ownership as well as installation

Keep separate lines for electricity, servicing, connectivity subscriptions and repairs. Ask for the installed equipment’s maintenance instructions and the proposed service scope. Visit charges, replacement parts and labour outside a service agreement can affect your later spending.

For electricity, obtain the standby power, operating demand and expected usage for the proposed equipment. Energy in kWh equals power in watts divided by 1,000, multiplied by hours of use. Calculate standby and active use separately and apply your own tariff without counting the same operating time twice. Include intercoms and other powered accessories if their demand is separate.

For a chosen ownership period, add installation, electricity, service visits, subscription charges and any repair allowances. Treat repair allowances as your planning assumptions rather than predictions. There is no reliable single annual cost for all gate systems.

Ask what each warranty covers, whether it includes labour and the conditions for making a claim. Gate material, coating, motors and workmanship may have different terms. Do not assume insurance discounts, resale gains or savings from a new system; check any relevant policy with your insurer and compare actual quotations. If an existing system is unreliable, request a repair assessment before deciding to replace it.

Prepare an enquiry that helps us quote

Send your area or postcode, photographs from both sides of the entrance and a description of how you want to use it. Include approximate dimensions if you have them, the current gate type, any known power supply and whether you want a pedestrian entrance. A survey is still needed to establish the final specification.

Tell us which matters most to you: privacy, appearance, vehicle access or easier daily use. Mention a budget if you have one so we can discuss the scope before developing a proposal.

Request a gate quotation and ask for the items above in writing. Keep the quotation, drawing, agreed changes, handover documents and maintenance instructions together for future reference.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much do electric driveway gates cost installed in London?+
The total depends on the measured entrance, gate specification, supports, groundworks, power and controls. Ask for a site-specific itemised quotation. A gate-only or motor-kit price is not a complete installed price.
Is automating existing gates cheaper than replacing them?+
It depends on what can be retained. An assessment may identify repairs or changes to the gate and supports before automation. Compare a written retrofit scope with a replacement quotation rather than assuming that keeping the leaves makes the whole job cheaper.
Should the quote include VAT?+
Ask the supplier to state whether VAT applies, the rate used and the final amount payable. Do not compare a VAT-exclusive figure with an inclusive total.
What ongoing costs should I allow for?+
Allow for electricity, maintenance, any connectivity subscriptions and repairs outside warranty or service cover. Use the proposed equipment details, your tariff and written service terms instead of a generic annual estimate.
Can you give a price from photographs?+
Photographs and approximate dimensions help us understand the enquiry. The measured opening, supports, power route and proposed scope still need assessment before a final quotation.

Home/Guides/Electric Gate Running Costs: Calculate Your Electricity Use
Updated 2 October 2026

Electric Gate Running Costs: Calculate Your Electricity Use

Estimate annual gate electricity use from movement time, standby demand and your own electricity tariff.

On this page +
Measure two different loadsA worked example with explicit unitsAdapt the calculation to your gateElectricity is only part of ownership cost

Measure two different loads

A gate uses electricity while moving and may also draw power while waiting. The controller, intercom, access receiver, network equipment and battery charger can contribute to that waiting load. Motor output ratings alone do not give the electricity drawn by the complete entrance.

Ask for measured input power or manufacturer consumption figures for the specified equipment. For two motors, use the combined demand. Record the total powered movement time for opening and closing, rather than treating an opening as a complete cycle.

A worked example with explicit units

This is an illustration, not a typical installation or a current tariff quote. Assume the complete system draws 100 W while moving and 5 W while idle. It makes ten complete cycles per day, each with 20 seconds of total powered movement.

Annual movement time = 20 × 10 × 365 ÷ 3,600 = 20.28 hours. Movement electricity = 0.100 kW × 20.28 hours = 2.03 kWh.

A 365-day year contains 8,760 hours. Idle time = 8,760 − 20.28 = 8,739.72 hours. Idle electricity = 0.005 kW × 8,739.72 hours = 43.70 kWh. Total electricity = 45.73 kWh. At an example tariff of £0.30 per kWh, that is £13.72 per year.

Adapt the calculation to your gate

Use annual kWh = (moving watts × moving hours + idle watts × idle hours) ÷ 1,000. Multiply the result by your unit tariff in pounds per kWh. Use 8,784 hours for a leap year.

The example treats moving power as the whole system demand during movement, so it subtracts movement time from idle time. If your motor figure is an additional load above a separately measured continuous baseline, calculate that baseline over the whole year instead. Do not count the same load twice.

If a cycle takes 40 seconds instead of 20, change the movement time before calculating both parts. Heaters, lighting and accessories that switch separately need their own power-and-time calculations.

Electricity is only part of ownership cost

SIM plans, cloud subscriptions, servicing, replacement batteries and repairs are separate costs. Ask which apply to the proposed equipment and whether VAT is included. An existing household electricity standing charge is not usually an additional gate cost; a separate metered supply could introduce one.

Keep electricity estimates separate from maintenance budgets when using our installed gate cost guide. For a retrofit, compare the work described in our automation quotation guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is 100 W for 20 seconds, ten times a day, 20.3 kWh per year?+
No. Under those assumptions it is about 2.03 kWh per year. Standby and other equipment must be calculated separately.
Is the example my likely bill?+
No. Replace the sample power, operating time and tariff with figures for your own system.

Home/Guides/Electric Gate Force Testing: What Homeowners Should Ask
Updated 2 October 2026

Electric Gate Force Testing: What Homeowners Should Ask

Understand what force testing can show, how it fits into a gate safety assessment and which records to request from a competent engineer.

On this page +
What force testing measuresWhere testing fits into the safety assessmentWhy one force number is not enoughWhat to request in the reportWhen to arrange an assessmentLeave adjustments and powered tests to a competent personFAQs

What force testing measures

Force testing measures forces produced when a moving gate encounters a test instrument under specified conditions. An engineer uses the results to assess the relevant protection and to establish a record for later checks. A person pushing against the gate cannot provide an equivalent measurement.

The appropriate procedure depends on the gate, its movement and the protective approach used. This guide explains the questions to ask; it does not provide a test procedure or a set of universal pass values.

Where testing fits into the safety assessment

Force limitation is one possible part of a gate’s protective measures. Where the installation relies on it, the installer needs to verify its performance. Other risks can require different measures, and an acceptable reading at one test point does not establish that the whole entrance is safe.

The assessment also needs to consider trapping and shearing areas, access to moving parts, the people using the entrance and foreseeable behaviour. Read our guide to photocells, edges and loops to understand why devices have different roles.

Why one force number is not enough

Force limits and test methods relate to defined conditions, positions and time periods. Presenting a number as a continuous safe pressure, or assuming the same value applies at every edge, loses that context. Do not use a simplified web table to approve an installation.

Ask the engineer which current standard or other technical approach supports the assessment, which risks the tests address and how the results will be recorded. They should have the competence and equipment for the work. Changes to force or sensitivity settings should not be a homeowner troubleshooting step.

What to request in the report

Ask the report to identify the entrance and equipment, the date and person doing the work, the checks undertaken, any limitations, findings and required actions. Where force tests are relevant, request the recorded results and their assessment in context.

Keep these records with the user instructions and handover documents. A statement that the gate opens and closes is not a substitute for a safety assessment. If an unsafe condition is identified, ask how the entrance should be kept out of use and what must happen before it can operate again.

When to arrange an assessment

Arrange advice after damage, unexpected movement, a suspected failure of a protective function or a change to the gate or drive. Follow the checking arrangements specified for your system. The requirements for a business or rented property may differ from those of a privately owned domestic entrance.

See our responsibilities guide. Avoid treating a fixed annual date as either a complete safety guarantee or a universal statutory requirement for all private homeowners.

Leave adjustments and powered tests to a competent person

Do not test the closing force with your body, a pet, a vehicle or improvised objects. Keep people clear if you suspect a fault and follow the supplied instructions for taking the gate out of use, provided that can be done safely.

Request a gate assessment and agree the inspection scope before booking. Sources: HSE guidance on powered-gate safety and HSE guidance on responsibilities.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does one passing force reading mean the gate is safe?+
No. A reading relates to particular conditions and locations. The complete entrance and its other hazards and protective measures still need assessment.
Can I test a gate by pushing against it?+
No. Do not use a person or improvised obstruction as a force-test instrument. Ask a competent engineer to carry out the appropriate assessment with suitable equipment.
Do all powered gates use the same protection and test procedure?+
No. The gate, environment, foreseeable users and protective approach determine what must be assessed and verified. Where force limitation is used, its performance needs suitable verification.

Home/Guides/How to Manually Open an Electric Gate During a Power Cut
Updated 2 October 2026

How to Manually Open an Electric Gate During a Power Cut

Find the correct manual-release instructions for your gate and understand when to stop and ask for help instead of forcing it open.

On this page +
Start with the instructions supplied for your gateCheck whether releasing it could allow uncontrolled movementLocate the release without dismantling the operatorFollow the model-specific isolation and release sequenceBefore returning to automatic operationPrepare for the next power interruptionFAQs

Start with the instructions supplied for your gate

Manual release arrangements differ between operators. Find the user instructions for your installed system and the release training provided at handover. Check the model from records or an identification label only where you can see it safely.

This guide cannot supply a universal key direction, cover-opening sequence or release position. If the instructions or key are missing, contact the installer or a competent gate engineer before attempting to release the mechanism.

Check whether releasing it could allow uncontrolled movement

Keep people, pets and vehicles away from the gate’s movement area. A gate freed from its drive may move because of a slope, wind or its own weight. Damage to hinges, supports or running gear can make manual movement unsafe.

Do not release a leaning, derailed, damaged or unstable gate. If you cannot control and secure it using the supplied instructions, keep clear and seek assistance. If someone is trapped or faces immediate danger, call the emergency services.

Locate the release without dismantling the operator

A surface-mounted operator may have a release on its housing. An underground swing-gate system may use a release arrangement near the gate or foundation box. A sliding system may have a release associated with its operator. The exact location and access method depend on the product.

Use the manufacturer’s diagram for your model. Do not open electrical enclosures, remove guards or disconnect drive components to search for a release. A key from another system may not fit or operate it correctly.

Follow the model-specific isolation and release sequence

Follow the supplied instructions for isolating power and preventing automatic operation before release. A mains power cut does not establish that every part is unpowered: the installation may have a backup battery or another supply.

Only operate the release and move the gate if the instructions and conditions allow you to do so safely. Use the specified method of holding or securing it. Do not force a seized key, lever or gate. Stop if movement is uneven, unexpectedly heavy or uncontrolled.

Before returning to automatic operation

Use the manufacturer’s instructions for securing the gate, re-engaging the drive and restoring operation. Keep the movement area clear. If the original problem was a mechanical fault rather than a power cut, restoring the supply does not resolve it.

If you are unsure whether the mechanism has re-engaged or the gate behaves differently, stop using it and arrange an assessment. Do not bypass sensors or repeatedly trigger the motor to make it reconnect.

Prepare for the next power interruption

Keep the correct key accessible to authorised users and store the instructions where they can be found. Ask the installer to demonstrate release and explain when it must not be attempted. Agree how people can use the entrance during a fault.

Backup capacity depends on the product, battery condition, accessories and use. Ask for the actual specification rather than a fixed cycle count. For a stuck mechanism, request gate repair assistance. See HSE guidance on responsibilities for user information and release arrangements.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is the manual release on my gate?+
Check the user instructions for the exact operator. Surface, underground and sliding systems can have different release arrangements. Do not dismantle equipment to look for one.
What if I have lost the release key?+
Contact the installer or a gate engineer with the safely obtained equipment details. Do not force the lock or assume that another model’s key is suitable.
Will the gate work during a power cut?+
Only if the installed system has a suitable backup arrangement and it can support the required use. Runtime varies; check the actual specification and condition.
The gate is hard to move after release. Should I push harder?+
No. Stop, keep the area clear and ask for assistance. Resistance or uncontrolled movement can indicate a mechanical or structural problem.

Updated 2 October 2026

Gate Safety Devices: Photocells, Safety Edges and Loops

Understand the different roles and limits of gate photocells, safety edges and vehicle loops, and why the whole entrance needs assessment.

On this page +
Start with the hazards at the entranceWhat photocells can detectWhat safety edges doWhat vehicle loops doPositioning and testing must suit the systemWhat owners should do when something changesFAQs

Start with the hazards at the entrance

Safety devices perform different functions. A gate can have several devices fitted and still present an unaddressed trapping or crushing risk. The installer needs to assess the complete gate, its movement, nearby structures and the people who may encounter it.

Ask the proposal to explain the risks identified and how the design addresses them. Do not treat a shopping list of sensors as a substitute for that assessment.

What photocells can detect

A photocell arrangement detects interruption of a beam or detection path. The area it covers depends on its design and positioning. A single beam does not detect every person or object anywhere around the gate.

The control system’s response depends on the equipment and configuration. Do not assume every beam interruption always causes the same stop or reversal in every operating direction. Ask the installer to explain the intended response and user checks.

What safety edges do

A suitable safety edge can detect contact along the area it protects and signal the control system. Selection, positioning, compatibility and the response of the complete system matter. Fitting an edge to one part of a gate does not establish protection at every other trapping point.

Ask which hazards the edges address and how their function will be verified. Damaged, loose or disconnected protection needs competent attention. Do not defeat a device to keep using the gate.

What vehicle loops do

An inductive loop detects a change caused by a suitable vehicle within its detection area. Depending on the design, it may form part of an access-control or vehicle-presence arrangement.

Do not rely on a vehicle loop to detect a pedestrian or provide all necessary protection. The installer must consider people on foot, cyclists, visitors and others alongside vehicle use. A convenient opening trigger and a safety function are not automatically interchangeable.

Positioning and testing must suit the system

There is no mounting height or device combination in this article that can approve every entrance. Gate geometry, surroundings, users and operating arrangements affect the specification. A competent installer needs to verify the proposed protective measures before handover.

Where force limitation is part of the protection, suitable verification is needed. Read our force-testing guide rather than attempting a test with your body or an improvised obstacle.

What owners should do when something changes

Follow the user instructions for routine checks and cleaning. Report visible damage, unexpected movement or a suspected failure of protection. Keep people clear and follow isolation instructions where you can do so safely.

Have a competent person assess faults and changes, including changes to the surrounding entrance. Keep records and ask when the gate can return to use. See HSE guidance on powered-gate safety, or request a gate assessment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will photocells detect everyone around a gate?+
No. Detection is limited to the arrangement’s coverage and operating conditions. Other hazards and people outside that area still need to be considered in the assessment.
Can a vehicle loop replace pedestrian protection?+
Do not assume that it can. A loop’s vehicle-detection function does not establish protection for people on foot. The complete entrance needs an appropriate safety assessment.
Can I bypass a faulty sensor temporarily?+
No. Stop using the affected system and obtain competent assistance. A bypass can remove protection that the installation relies on.

Home/Guides/Swing vs Sliding Driveway Gates
Updated 2 October 2026

Swing vs Sliding Driveway Gates

Compare parking clearance, side space, slopes and everyday access before choosing how your driveway gate opens.

On this page +
Measure the space each leaf occupiesAllow for the full sliding arrangementSlopes and drainage can change the choiceChoose around daily use

Measure the space each leaf occupies

A swing leaf travels around its hinge. For an illustrative pair of equal leaves across a 3.5 m opening, each leaf is about 1.75 m wide before allowing for gaps and fittings. Its free edge traces an arc with roughly that radius, rather than the full 3.5 m opening width.

That arithmetic is not a safe parking distance. Hinge position, opening angle, vehicle shape, pedestrian routes and protective clearances determine the usable space. Ask for a scaled plan showing the gate in motion and your car parked.

Allow for the full sliding arrangement

A sliding gate moves beside the entrance. The gate needs room along that path, including its supporting arrangement and safe separation from walls, fences and people. Cantilever designs have a supporting tail; tracked and multi-panel systems have different space requirements.

A car may be able to park beyond the sliding path, but the survey still needs to consider turning, waiting and pedestrian access. Read about telescopic options if side space is limited.

Slopes and drainage can change the choice

A rising driveway can obstruct a swing leaf. A sliding layout also needs a suitable travel path, supports and drainage. Neither layout becomes suitable simply by adding a stronger motor.

Share measured levels and any flooding history with the installer. Our sloping-driveway guide explains the questions to resolve before ordering.

Choose around daily use

Consider where visitors stop, how pedestrians enter, and how bins and deliveries pass the gate. Ask how you will operate the entrance during a power cut and what maintenance access the design needs.

Compare swing-gate installation with sliding-gate installation using the same design and access requirements. Groundworks and the complete specification determine cost; there is no fixed percentage difference that applies to every site.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a pair of gates need the entire opening width behind it?+
Each leaf has its own swept arc. Use the actual leaf dimensions and a site drawing that also accounts for vehicles, people and protective clearances.
Which is better for a short driveway?+
A sliding or folding design may help, but side space, supports, gradient and safe movement still need assessment.

Home/Guides/UK Electric Gate Safety: Responsibilities and Handover
Updated 2 October 2026

UK Electric Gate Safety: Responsibilities and Handover

Understand installer responsibilities, conformity documents and the difference between private-home and workplace gate maintenance duties.

On this page +
The completed entrance mattersInstaller and manufacturer responsibilitiesCE and UKCA marking in Great BritainPrivate homes, workplaces and landlordsTesting, maintenance and changesA practical handover checklistFAQs

The completed entrance matters

A powered gate is a machine. Its safety depends on the assembled gate, supports, drive, controls, protective measures and surroundings. A marked motor or a list of fitted sensors does not by itself demonstrate that the complete installation is safe.

A site assessment should consider the people who can encounter the gate, including visitors and children, and the places where movement could cause injury. The proposal and handover should explain how the identified risks are addressed.

Installer and manufacturer responsibilities

HSE explains that the person assembling a powered gate from components can become the manufacturer of the completed machine. Converting an existing manual gate to power operation can also create these responsibilities.

Ask who will take responsibility for the completed installation. Request the Declaration of Conformity, user instructions and the recommended maintenance and safety checks at handover. A component manual or motor receipt is not a substitute for the documents for the assembled gate.

CE and UKCA marking in Great Britain

Do not rely on the claim that CE marking stopped being accepted for gate equipment in January 2023. Current government guidance describes CE recognition alongside or in place of UKCA for relevant product regimes in Great Britain. The applicable rules depend on the product and market.

Ask the supplier to identify the conformity route and documents for the equipment and completed installation. See GOV.UK guidance on UKCA or CE marked products. Northern Ireland has separate arrangements.

Private homes, workplaces and landlords

HSE distinguishes private domestic owners from people responsible for gates at work or as part of a work activity. Its guidance says health and safety law does not apply to owners of gates on privately owned domestic premises, while recommending regular checks. This does not remove product or installer obligations, or a householder’s potential liability for harm or damage.

Commercial owners, employers, landlords and managing agents can have duties to keep gates safe. If your entrance serves rented property, a shared development or a business, establish who is responsible for its operation, maintenance and records. Do not use advice for a single private home as the complete answer for those settings.

Testing, maintenance and changes

The installer needs to assess and check the completed system before handover. Where force limitation forms part of the protection, its performance needs suitable verification. Read our force-testing explanation for what a homeowner should ask.

Follow the installation’s instructions and maintenance recommendations. Do not assume that one annual visit or a generic device list proves continuing safety. Report damage, unexpected movement or failed protective functions and seek competent help. Significant modifications may require a new conformity assessment; straightforward servicing is not automatically the same situation.

A practical handover checklist

Ask for the gate and equipment identification, operating instructions, manual-release training, isolation information, conformity documents and the recommended checking arrangements. Keep the responsible company’s contact details and agree what to do if a fault makes the entrance unsafe.

For an existing installation with missing records, request a gate assessment. Agree what the visit can establish rather than expect a certificate from photographs. Source: HSE guidance on responsibilities.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is UKCA the only acceptable marking for gate equipment in Great Britain?+
No blanket statement applies to every product. Current government guidance recognises CE alongside or in place of UKCA for relevant regimes. Ask the supplier to confirm the applicable route and documentation.
Must a private homeowner have an annual gate test by law?+
HSE distinguishes private domestic ownership from work and landlord responsibilities and recommends regular checks for domestic gates. Follow the installation instructions and obtain advice for your actual circumstances rather than assuming a universal annual legal rule.
What should I receive at handover?+
Request the completed system’s conformity documents, user instructions, operating and release training, and recommendations for maintenance and safety checks.

Home/Guides/Winter Gate Maintenance for London Homes
Updated 2 October 2026

Winter Gate Maintenance for London Homes

Prepare your entrance for wet and cold weather with safe observations, the right service records and a clear fault plan.

On this page +
Check the entrance before colder weatherKeep homeowner care within the instructionsWhat to discuss at a service visitPrepare for a power cut or breakdown

Check the entrance before colder weather

From outside the movement area, look for damaged fittings, a leaning leaf, unusual gaps, standing water or debris near tracks and drains. Note changes in noise or movement during normal use. Do not repeat a faulty movement to investigate it.

Keep the gate instructions, service records and installer contact details together. Arrange an assessment before winter if the gate scrapes, hesitates or behaves differently. Tell the engineer about flooding, impact damage or recent paving work.

Keep homeowner care within the instructions

Carry out only the cleaning and care described for your installed system, using its stated isolation arrangements. Keep hands clear of hinges, rollers and trapping points. Do not remove electrical covers, change force settings or bypass sensors.

Lubricant type and application points depend on the equipment. Adding oil or grease to an unsuitable part can create problems. Ice, compacted debris and water in a motor enclosure need assessment; do not use force or improvised heat to restore operation.

What to discuss at a service visit

Ask the engineer to inspect the mechanical condition, supports, drainage, cabling and protective measures relevant to your entrance. Discuss how weather exposure and use affect the maintenance schedule. Request a record of findings, remedial work and checks before return to use.

Confirm the visit charge and what it covers before booking. Ask how parts or additional work will be authorised. A seasonal checklist cannot replace the maintenance instructions or an assessment of the complete system.

Prepare for a power cut or breakdown

Check that you have the correct user instructions and release key, and understand how the gate would be controlled and secured. Wind and gravity can move a released gate. Battery backup, where fitted, needs its own maintenance and capacity checks.

Read our manual-release guide before an emergency. If the motor hums without moving, stop repeated attempts and use our fault information checklist when requesting a repair assessment.

Further reading: HSE powered-gate safety and maintenance guidance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should every gate be serviced once a year?+
Follow the system instructions and an engineer’s assessment of use, condition and exposure. A calendar interval alone does not establish that a gate is safe.
Can I increase the motor force in cold weather?+
Do not change safety or force settings to overcome a fault. Stop using a gate that struggles and arrange assessment.

How much do driveway gates cost in London?+

The total depends on the measured entrance, gate material and design, supports, groundworks, electrical supply and manual or automated operation. Request an itemised quotation with VAT, exclusions and payment terms stated.

Do I need planning permission for driveway gates in London?+

Check the proposed height, position beside a highway, listed status, conservation-area controls, any Article 4 direction and planning conditions with the relevant authority. The rules depend on the property and work; opening inward alone does not establish permission.

How long does a driveway gate installation take?+

The programme depends on fabrication, supports, groundworks, electrical work and the agreed gate specification. Ask for the proposed lead time and installation schedule in your written quotation.

What type of gate is best for a London driveway?+

The survey should compare movement space, gradient, supports, parking and pedestrian access alongside your preferred appearance. The suitable material and opening layout depend on the complete entrance.

Can I automate my existing manual gates?+

Possibly, after assessment of the gate, supports, movement, surrounding hazards and proposed equipment. Ask what repairs or alterations are needed and compare the complete retrofit scope before buying motors.

Do you supply the gates as well as install them?+

We design, supply and install driveway gates and also discuss automation, repairs and maintenance. The written quotation will set out the agreed products, work, exclusions and handover arrangements.

Are electric gates safe for children and pets?+

A powered entrance needs a site-specific assessment, suitable protective measures and checks of the completed system. Children and pets must be considered in that assessment. A generic list of sensors does not by itself establish safety.

What happens if there is a power cut?+

Follow the user instructions for your installed system. Manual release and backup arrangements differ by product, and releasing a gate can allow uncontrolled movement. If you are unsure how to operate and secure it safely, keep clear and seek assistance.

ANPR Gate Entry Systems

Number-plate entry planned around camera position, authorised vehicles, safe waiting and access-data management.

DetailsFAQsGet a quote

Plan the approach and fallback

ANPR reads a vehicle registration and checks it against access permissions. It does not establish who is driving or prevent a second vehicle following the first. Decide where the driver waits and how entry works if a plate is not read.

Do not assume a vehicle can drive through without stopping. Camera recognition, the command to the controller and safe gate movement are separate parts of the sequence. Include visitors, deliveries and pedestrian access in the plan.

Check recognition at the actual entrance

Survey camera position, approach angle, lighting, headlight glare, stopping distance and the expected plate types. Ask the supplier to demonstrate the proposed equipment under the conditions that matter at your site.

A manufacturer’s performance figure under defined test conditions is not a guarantee for every vehicle or weather condition. Agree a keypad, intercom or other authorised fallback.

Manage permissions and records

Decide who can add, remove and review authorised registrations. Confirm expiry for temporary vehicles, administrator access and account recovery. Ask whether the system records images or events, where it stores them and how long it keeps them.

Where data-protection law applies, the operator must address the purpose, lawful use, notice, retention and access controls. Consult ICO video-surveillance guidance. A product label does not make the whole installation compliant.

Specify the complete installation

Include camera and controller models, network and power, gate interface, subscriptions, commissioning and user training. Confirm ongoing support and the effect of connection or power failure.

Compare video entry and keypads for visitors. Send your entrance layout and expected use when you discuss your entrance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will ANPR read every plate?+
Recognition depends on the camera, setup, approach, lighting, plate condition and supported plate formats. Test the actual proposal and agree a fallback.
Can cars enter without stopping?+
Do not assume this. The design must provide a suitable approach and waiting arrangement while recognition and safe gate movement take place.
Does ANPR replace gate safety devices?+
No. Permission to enter is separate from the protective measures and checks required for the powered entrance.

Hand over account control

Is phone entry independent of power and broadband?+
It may not need home broadband, but the gate and phone-entry equipment still need power and the required mobile service.
Are opening calls free?+
That depends on how the product handles calls and the applicable tariffs. Confirm the charges rather than assuming a missed-call arrangement.
